The full workings live in `02-community-composition.qmd` (ordination and
PERMANOVA) and `03-bv-by-arm.qmd` (the BV check). This page is the version
to present: the answer, the two figures that carry it, and the numbers
behind it.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(microViz)
library(phyloseq)

source(here("R/count_tables.R"))

dd <- read_counts("group_b")
ps <- as_counts("group_b", "microbiome", data = dd)
psb <- ps |> tax_transform("compositional") |> dist_calc("bray")

# helper: run a PERMANOVA for arm, return its R2 and p
arm_result <- function(ps_obj) {
  t <- as.data.frame(perm_get(
    ps_obj |> dist_permanova(variables = "arm", n_perms = 999, seed = 202, verbose = FALSE)
  ))
  tibble(r2 = round(t$R2[1], 3), p = t[["Pr(>F)"]][1])
}
```

## The answer

**No — contraceptive method explains almost none of the variation in these
vaginal communities (~3%, p ≈ 0.15). What does explain it is BV status
(~14%, p = 0.001), and BV is spread evenly across the arms. The one
suggestive exception is pill vs injectable (p ≈ 0.03, but ≈ 0.10 once the
three comparisons are corrected for), which agrees with a
simple biology check and is tomorrow's lead.**

## Figure 1 — the map: three overlapping crowds, not three islands

Each point is one participant's vaginal community. Bray-Curtis PCoA: points
close together have similar communities.

```{r}
psb |> ord_calc("PCoA") |> ord_plot(colour = "arm") +
  labs(title = "Bray-Curtis PCoA, coloured by contraceptive method")
```

The same points, coloured by what actually separates them:

```{r}
psb |> ord_calc("PCoA") |> ord_plot(colour = "bv") +
  labs(title = "… coloured by BV status")
```

## Figure 2 — BV is everywhere, in every arm

BV prevalence by arm; Fisher's exact test p ≈ 0.45 (details in
`03-bv-by-arm.qmd`). No arm is protected or penalised.

```{r}
dd$metadata |>
  count(arm, bv) |>
  ggplot(aes(arm, n, fill = bv)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of samples", fill = "BV status",
       title = "BV status by contraceptive arm")
```

## The evidence, in one table

```{r}
# overall PERMANOVA: the full multi-variable model, so row 1 = arm, row 2 = bv
overall  <- psb |> dist_permanova(variables = c("arm", "bv", "ph", "any_sti", "rnaseq_batch"),
                                  n_perms = 999, seed = 202, by = "margin")
ov       <- as.data.frame(perm_get(overall))
arm_r2   <- round(ov$R2[1], 3);  arm_p <- ov[["Pr(>F)"]][1]
bv_r2    <- round(ov$R2[2], 3);  bv_p  <- ov[["Pr(>F)"]][2]

# pairwise: pill vs injectable
ids <- dd$metadata$sample_id[dd$metadata$arm %in% c("pill", "injectable")]
pw  <- arm_result(prune_samples(ids, ps) |> tax_transform("compositional") |> dist_calc("bray"))

# sensitivity: drop the nine low-depth samples (< 15,000 reads)
lib <- tibble(sample_id = dd$metadata$sample_id, reads = colSums(dd$species))
sens <- arm_result(
  prune_samples(setdiff(dd$metadata$sample_id, lib$sample_id[lib$reads < 15000]), ps) |>
    tax_transform("compositional") |> dist_calc("bray"))

# lactobacillus share by arm
tax <- dd$taxonomy
lacto <- colSums(dd$species[tax$Genus == "Lactobacillus", ]) / colSums(dd$species)
lacto_md <- dd$metadata |>
  mutate(lacto = lacto[sample_id]) |>
  group_by(arm) |> summarise(median = median(lacto))

arm_alone <- arm_result(psb)

tibble(
  claim = c("Arm alone",
            "Arm after BV, pH, STI and batch are accounted for",
            "BV status's share of the variation between samples",
            "Pill vs injectable, tested alone",
            "Same overall test, 9 low-depth samples dropped",
            "Lactobacillus share, pill vs other arms (median)"),
  number = c(
    paste0("R² = ", arm_alone$r2, ", p = ", arm_alone$p),
    paste0("R² = ", arm_r2, ", p = ", round(arm_p, 3)),
    paste0("R² = ", bv_r2, ", p = ", bv_p),
    paste0("R² = ", pw$r2, ", p = ", pw$p),
    paste0("R² = ", sens$r2, ", p = ", sens$p),
    paste0(scales::percent(lacto_md$median[lacto_md$arm == "pill"], 0.1),
           " vs ",
           scales::percent(median(lacto_md$median[lacto_md$arm != "pill"]), 0.1))),
  evidence = c("PERMANOVA, `02-community-composition`",
               "PERMANOVA, `02-community-composition`",
               "PERMANOVA, `02-community-composition`",
               "Pairwise PERMANOVA, `02-community-composition`",
               "Sensitivity analysis, `02-community-composition`",
               "Biology check, `02-community-composition`")
) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Claim", "Number", "Where it comes from"))
```

## The one-liner for the slides

> Overall, no: method explains ~3% of the variation in community
> composition (p ≈ 0.15); BV explains ~14% and is evenly spread across arms
> (p ≈ 0.45). Pill vs injectable is the suggestive exception (p ≈ 0.03,
> ≈ 0.10 after Holm correction; Lactobacillus share 85% vs ~45%) — chase it
> with the gene table.

## Choices made

- All methods, thresholds and seeds are inherited from the two full reports
  (`02-community-composition.qmd`, `03-bv-by-arm.qmd`); nothing was
  re-decided here — this page only re-presents them.
- Main distance **Bray-Curtis on relative abundances** (compositional
  transform), matching `02-community-composition.qmd`; Aitchison and Jaccard
  agreed in the full report and are not repeated here.
- **999 permutations, seed 202** for every PERMANOVA on this page.
- Figures shown are **arm-coloured and BV-coloured PCoA** plus the BV bar
  chart; alternatives (pH, STI, batch panels) are in the full report and
  changed nothing.
- The evidence table **recomputes** the numbers with the same seeds rather
  than copy-pasting them, so it would visibly disagree if the underlying
  reports were changed.
